front.text: V tiskom jsem zdieľal kufor s kolegom, ale on ho posielil do nového mesta.

back.text: I shared my suitcase with a colleague, but he sent it to a new city.
back.notes:
v tskim jsem zdieľal kufor s kolegom, ale on ho posielil do nového mesta.

kufor is the accusative form of 'kufor' (suitcase), serving as the direct object of the verb 'zdieľal' (shared).

tsikom

Discovered in: V tiskom jsem zdieľal kufor s kolegom, ale on ho posielil do nového mesta.

front.text: Vy a vaša kolegyňa idete na pohár?

back.text: You and your colleague are going for a drink?
back.notes:
[vi a ˈvaʃa ˈkɔleɡiɲa ˈɪdete na ˈpɔhaːr]

The pronoun 'Vy' is the formal or plural 'you', serving as the subject of the sentence alongside 'vaša kolegyňa'.

front.text: Angličan Tom kupoval čerstvý chleb v trhu.

back.text: The English man Tom bought fresh bread at the market.
back.notes:
Angličan Tom kupoval čerstvý chleb v trhu

Angličan is the masculine singular noun indicating a male national from the United Kingdom, serving as the subject of the sentence.

front.text: Slovák Štefan kľúčom otvoril dve vrátania.

back.text: The Slovak Štefan opened two doors with a key.
back.notes:
Slovák Štefan kľúčom otvoril dve vrátania

Slovák is the nominative masculine singular noun denoting a person of Slovak ethnic origin, serving as the subject of the sentence.

back.text: The girl is reading a book on the street.
back.notes:
[ˈdʲevtʃa ˈtʃiːta ˈknɪxu na ˈulɪtsi]

The noun 'Dievča' is a neuter singular word meaning 'girl', serving as the subject of the sentence.

back.text: I see a child in front of the cafe.
back.notes:
[ˈdɪecɐ]

The noun "dieťa" (child) is a neuter noun in the accusative singular, which is identical to the nominative singular. It functions as the direct object of the verb "vidím" (I see).

front.text: Nemohla som to povedať tak dobre ako ty.

back.text: I couldn't say it as well as you.
back.notes:
[tak ˈdɔbrɛ]

Príslovcové spojenie „tak dobre“ znamená „tak veľmi dobre“; „tak“ zosilňuje príslovku „dobre“.

front.text: Peter prišiel, ale on už odišiel.

back.text: Peter came, but he has already left.
back.notes:
[ɔn]

Osobné zámeno v nominatíve jednotného čísla mužského rodu; v tejto vete odkazuje na Petra.

[to]

“To” is a neuter singular nominative demonstrative pronoun meaning “that.” It is the subject pointing to something being indicated.

[ja]

The personal pronoun “I” in the nominative singular, used as the emphasized subject.

front.text: Slovenka Ana spravila na mieste konci knihy.

back.text: The Slovak woman Ana finished the book at the place.
back.notes:
Slovenka Ana spravila na mieste konci knihy

Slovenka is the feminine singular noun indicating a woman of Slovenian origin, functioning as the subject of the sentence.

[ˈt͡ʃakaː]

čaká is the third-person singular present form of čakať, meaning is waiting; čakať na plus the accusative names the person or thing waited for.

back.text: They are going to the cafe.
back.notes:
[ˈɔni ˈɪduː ˈda kaviˈarne]

The pronoun 'Oni' is the masculine plural 'they', acting as the subject of the sentence.

/taɪ/

Ty means “you” and is the singular nominative subject of the sentence.

back.text: They are going for ice cream.
back.notes:
[ˈɔni ˈɪduː na ˈzmrzlɪna]

The pronoun 'Ony' is the feminine or neuter plural 'they', acting as the subject of the sentence.

[maːm]

The word "Mám" is the first-person singular present tense of the verb "mať" (to have), meaning "I have" in this sentence.

front.text: Američan Mike povedal, že ho miluje jeho rodina.

back.text: The American man Mike said that his family loves him.
back.notes:
Američan Mike povedal, že ho miluje jeho rodina

Američan is the masculine singular noun indicating a male national from the United States, serving as the subject of the sentence.
